task_instruction:
Persona:

	As a 41-year-old office administrator, you use your cellphone daily for both work and personal tasks. While you're familiar with common phone functions, you wouldn't call yourself a tech enthusiast.

	Your technical skills are average - you handle standard smartphone features like calls, texts, email, and basic apps with ease. You understand the fundamental settings, but prefer clear, step-by-step guidance when trying something new.

	In interactions, you're naturally friendly and patient. When receiving help, you listen attentively and aren't afraid to ask questions. You make sure to confirm your understanding and provide detailed feedback on each instruction you receive.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You mobile data is not working properly. It either stops working or is very slow. You want to fix it and absolutely want to get excellent internet speed on your phone. You are not willing to accept any other internet speed (poor, fair or good). You do not have access to wifi.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved only when speed test returns excellent internet speed and nothing else. If it returns poor, fair or good, you will not consider the issue resolved. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?

turns.thought: I'd be happy to help you get your mobile data working properly. To get started, could you please provide me with your phone number or account ID so I can look up your account?

turns.thought:
The **2 GB has been successfully added** to line L1002 (555-123-2002) for **$4.00** — you'll see this charge on your next bill.

Regarding speed: I've confirmed the data has been applied to your line, but I can't verify actual connection speed from my side. A few things to keep in mind as you head out:

- **You're in France**, so you're using a partner network abroad. Speeds there depend on that network and can be slower than at home, even with plenty of data. Your line's international roaming is already enabled.
- On your phone, please check your status bar for a signal/network indicator (e.g., 5G, LTE, 4G).
- Since you have no Wi-Fi, make sure **mobile data is turned on** and, importantly, that **Data Roaming is turned ON** on your device — without it, you won't connect abroad even though your line is roaming-enabled.
- Also check that **Airplane Mode is off** and **Data Saver is off**, as either can limit your connection.

If you make those checks and data is still slow or not working, message me back and we'll dig further into the device settings together. Your refreshed data (2 GB) is available right now and runs through the end of your cycle on **February 28**.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me check those things on my phone now.

turns.thought:
Thanks for the detailed report — that's very helpful. I can see your line itself is in good shape (Active, refueled data applied, international roaming enabled on my side), so the remaining issues are all on your device settings. Here's what to do, in this order:

**1. Turn Mobile Data ON**
This is the master switch — nothing will connect until it's on. Go to **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network**, and turn **Mobile Data** on.

**2. Turn Data Roaming ON**
Because you're in France on a partner network, this is required. In the same **Mobile Network** menu (or under *Roaming*), turn **Data Roaming** on. Your account already has international roaming enabled, so there's no charge for turning this on.

**3. Change your preferred network mode to 4G/5G**
You're currently stuck on **2G**, which is far too slow for data — and it also won't support picture messaging. Go to **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network → Preferred network mode / Network mode**, and select **5G/4G preferred** (often labelled "4G/5G auto" or "LTE/WCDMA"). Avoid 2G or 3G-only options.

**4. Turn Data Saver OFF**
Data Saver restricts background data and can make apps feel slow or unresponsive. Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → Data Saver** and turn it **off**.

**5. Restart your phone**
After changing network mode and APN-type settings, a reboot is needed for them to take effect. Power the phone off and back on.

**Once restarted**, please tell me:
- What the signal strength and network type show now (looking for 4G/5G instead of 2G)
- Whether **Mobile Data** and **Data Roaming** both show as on
- Whether you have a working internet connection, and roughly how fast it feels (try loading a web page)

One more note: you have a **VPN connected**. VPNs can sometimes cause significant slowdowns abroad. Let's first see how things perform after the steps above — if speeds are still poor, try temporarily disconnecting the VPN and re-testing, and let me know the difference.

Go ahead with steps 1–5 and report back what you see.
turns.execution_output: User: That's a lot of steps! I'll take them one at a time so I don't mess anything up — could you walk me through them one by one? Let me start with step 1: turning Mobile Data ON.

**Next: change your preferred network mode to 4G/5G.**

Go to **Settings → Network & Internet / Connections → Mobile Network → Preferred network mode** (may be called *Network mode* or *Preferred network type*), and select:

> **5G/4G preferred** — often labelled "5G/LTE auto", "4G/5G auto", or "LTE/WCDMA"

Make sure you do **not** pick a 2G-only or 3G-only option.

This is worth doing now, because 2G won't carry a usable data connection — and it also can't support picture/video messages.

Once you've selected it, **restart your phone** so the change takes effect. After the reboot, please report back:

- Signal strength (still Poor? better?)
- Network type (looking for **4G/LTE/5G** instead of 2G)
- Whether web pages now load, and roughly how fast

If after the reboot it's still stuck on 2G or speeds are poor, we'll look at your APN settings — and I'll also want to test with the VPN disconnected, since that can throttle things overseas too.

That's great news — Excellent signal and 5G already. Still, **yes, go ahead and restart** — the network-mode change (and any carrier settings refresh) settles in best after a reboot, and it makes sure everything holds rather than reverting.

**What to do:**

1. **Restart your phone** (power off, wait ~10 seconds, power back on).
2. After it comes back up, confirm the status bar still shows **5G**, **Data Enabled**, and Data Saver staying off.
3. **Test the connection** — try loading a web page or running a speed test, and tell me how it feels (fast / okay / still slow).

**One important variable: your VPN is still connected.** VPNs are a common cause of slow speeds abroad. So if things feel fast right now — leave it be and you're done. But if speeds are still disappointing after the reboot, please **temporarily disconnect the VPN** and re-test, then tell me whether it improved. That will tell us whether the VPN is the culprit.

Once you've rebooted and tested, report back:
- Network type after reboot (still 5G?)
- Whether data is working
- How the speed feels (and whether disconnecting the VPN changed anything)

If it's fast, you're all set — and your 2 GB refueled data is available through **February 28**.

Yes — that's exactly the right next move. Since the VPN is still connected and you're abroad, it's the most likely remaining cause of the gap between "Good" and "Excellent."

**What to do:**

1. **Disconnect the VPN.** Go to **Settings → Network & Internet → VPN** and toggle it off (or open your VPN app and tap Disconnect).
2. Confirm the status bar no longer shows the VPN icon.
3. **Run the speed test again** while the VPN is off.
4. Report the new number and label back to me.

**How to read the result:**

- If the speed jumps noticeably (e.g. to a higher tier like "Excellent") — the VPN was throttling your connection. You can leave it off while you want maximum speed, or switch to a VPN server closer to your location if you must keep it on.
- If the speed stays around the same 27.5 Mbps — then the VPN isn't the bottleneck, and the ceiling is likely the partner network you're connected to in France plus your 2G-poor-signal starting conditions before the fix.

One thing worth keeping in mind: your line is using a French partner network right now, so the maximum available speed depends partly on their local infrastructure and how busy the tower is — that's not something I can change from my side. I can only make sure your line and device are optimally configured, which they now are: 5G, Excellent signal, data on, roaming on, Data Saver off, and 2 GB of refueled data available through **February 28**.

Go ahead and re-test with the VPN off, and let me know what number you get.
